subject: Tenant traffic capture & attack-lattice — forensic capability packet
messages:
From: Jenna Carroll <jenna.carroll@orchidbank.com>

Cc: procurement@orchidbank.com
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 10:14:00 -0500
Subject: Tenant traffic capture and attack-lattice — initial request

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our external audit and ongoing contract work we need a clear statement of how Redwood handles on-demand tenant traffic capture and what forensic artifacts you can provide. Specifically: 

1) Can you produce sanitized PCAPs on request (chain of custody, redaction, delivery)?
2) What controls exist to ensure captures only contain traffic scoped to our tenant?
3) What is the SLA (time-to-deliver) and retention for captured artifacts?
4) Describe any post-capture analysis you can do (e.g., flow reconstruction, reassembly, timeline mapping).

We also want a short "attack lattice" summary mapping the most plausible cross-tenant and control-plane vectors and how capture + telemetry would help detect/forensically investigate them.

We can sign any specific data handling addenda required; the procurement team is on copy. Ideally we get a packet we can present to the auditor by early next week.

Thanks,
Jenna
Jenna Carroll
Head of Security — Orchid Bank
jenna.carroll@orchidbank.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, procurement@orchidbank.com

Subject: Re: Tenant traffic capture and attack-lattice — initial request

Hi Jenna — appreciate the clear ask. High-level answers below and I attached a concise packet with diagrams and a threat-lattice sketch (network-capture-process-v1.pdf, attack-lattice-v1.png). TL;DR: we can produce sanitized PCAPs, we scope captures to tenant ingress/egress and sidecar telemetry, and we provide an evidence bundle with checksums and transfer logs.

1) PCAP production and chain-of-custody
- We support on-demand capture requests for production tenant traffic that traverses the sidecar proxy or the egress gateway. Captures are performed at the capture layer (sidecar or egress hop) and written to an isolated staging bucket encrypted with a tenant-specific key.
- For audit requests we perform sanitization to remove data-plane payloads you designate (PII tokens, full request bodies). The sanitized PCAP is hashed (SHA-256) and we attach a signed manifest (timestamp + signer) to guarantee integrity.
- Delivery options: SFTP over a dedicated transfer node, or a SecureShare link with short-lived access tokens. We can notarize transfer events in our audit log.

2) Tenant scoping and isolation controls
- Capture points are limited to: (a) tenant-dedicated sidecars that see only that tenant's requests/response bytes; (b) tenant ingress VIPs and egress gateway flows. We do not capture cross-tenant mesh-internal control-plane chatter by default.
- Access controls: PCAP artifacts are only visible to RBAC roles marked "forensics" + the tenant's configured support contacts. All access is logged (actor, method, TTL).
- Logical evidence separation: captures are named with tenant-id, requestid, and sequence number; by default we include only 5 seconds pre-trigger and 5 seconds post-trigger unless you request expanded windows.

3) SLA and retention
- Standard SLA: 72 hours to produce a sanitized PCAP bundle after a formal request (template attached). Expedited option (24 hours) available under escalation with a one-off production fee.
- Retention: immediate staging for 90 days by default, then archival for 12 months on customer request. All retention is configurable in dedicated (contracted) deployments.

4) Post-capture analysis
- We can: extract flow records (NetFlow-style summaries), reassemble HTTP sessions, extract TLS session metadata (SNI, cert fingerprint), and provide timeline reconstructions mapped to our runtime traces (request routing, model variant, KV cache hits).
- We provide an "evidence bundle" containing: sanitized PCAP(s), flow summary CSV, signed manifest, and a short analyst note mapping timelines to internal trace-ids.

Notes on safety and impact
- Capture sampling: continuous capture at full rate is not enabled by default for prod due to cost/latency. We perform targeted captures by trigger (operator request or system-detected anomaly).
- Performance: capture at sidecar is zero-copy to an isolated buffer; writes can produce a small I/O spike to staging buckets. We coordinate maintenance windows if you expect frequent large captures.

Next steps:
- I've attached the capture-process packet and a 1-page attack-lattice diagram. Kimberly is copied to confirm operational SLAs; Vivek can chime on cryptographic custody and HSM logistics. If you want a sanitized sample PCAP for the auditor, say so and we'll generate one with dummy payloads and the manifest.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
[Attachments: network-capture-process-v1.pdf, attack-lattice-v1.png]

Subject: Re: Tenant traffic capture and attack-lattice — operational notes

Hi Jenna — adding operational specifics and the capture-request-template (attached). A few clarifications so auditors have precise expectations: 

- Production capture scope: by default our capture points are sidecar egress, tenant ingress balancer, and the inter-zone egress gateway. For Dedicated deployments we can enable an additional mirrored tap in the tenant VLAN.
- Sanitization policy: we apply rule-based redaction. The request template allows you to mark fields to redact (headers, request body JSON paths, cookie tokens). Redaction is performed before hashing to avoid exposing raw values.
- Chain of custody and custodianship: artifacts are issued with a signed manifest that includes a transfer log (user, ip, method). We store the manifest in the immutable audit ledger for 12 months. If you require HSM-backed signing, we can enable a KMS/attestation flow in Private deployments (Vivek can provide the HSM cert flow).
- Forensics delivery SLA: 72 hours standard. We will also provide a short analyst memo that maps PCAP timestamps to request/worker trace-ids for fast triage.

Operational impact & cost
- Large captures (>10GB) may require off-hours processing. We will flag potential latency impact during capture and propose a window if necessary.
- If Orchid Bank wants continuous high-fidelity capture, we recommend a contracted Dedicated pool to avoid noisy-neighbor cost and to maintain isolation.

Attached: capture-request-template.docx (formalizes the request fields and retention choices). I can join the auditor call on Monday if you want us to walk through the packet.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Customer Operations — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
[Attachment: capture-request-template.docx]
